restrictions: Messages of 55 and 63 bytes (the 63-byte one ends in eight zero bytes): one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and the true block length; unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision of two distinct complete messages.

winglock's c19feef (order S2K, 93.7358) with two changes by Subflatus3: stride 2^14 (order S2K14, from ef81f589) with premises measured again, and a pair test shared by two positions. From c19feef: order S2K (X2 table, Lemma A3), pass-flag tests (Lemmas A3, F2), 1-op budgets, the per-batch sample design, rtuni4.c and the program modified here; from winglock's 18a7fc52, d26a3c5f, 2bb5d604, 098e66f4, 21252124: S8, beta filter (Lemma B), Lemmas D and D', exact S8 count, block accumulator, stage C, a random word per outer step, exact stage values, Chernoff bound on budgets, D3.d1 = X3. c66f230d (Jbenisek, co-author tekkac): cancellation, constants, class, rule A, Lemma N. 60f94c5c (Jbenisek): three-level construction, table, staged batch with budgets. 52bb50ee and 1d5e54ce (Subflatus3): sampled run-average premise, Lemma C', Lemma U. 5266c5ce (leech1996): budgets 1/6000 above the premises. df8bd46d, 8c81a219 (Th0rgal); ticket 2bf40fb (tekkac). Co-authors: winglock, Jbenisek, tekkac, Th0rgal, leech1996.

Ours (Subflatus3 and us) in this version: F_H1 = 132,392,960 (margin 1.400, disclosed) and V = 1,057,885;  the stride 2^14 (C2.a1 = (7g + l) 2^14 + i, g < 37,450, i < 2^14; C2.d1 = i 2^16 + D with D = (r >> 2) + (r AND 3) 2^30 keeps Lemma A3 and the one-addition update), four D slots (D of group g + 4 = D of group g + 7), the last group of one distinct lane, a preregistered 2^35-batch uniform sample of this order with a decision rule at 2^-64 for both tests, and, new in this version, the pair test (Lemma P: positions i, i + 1 compute their flag words pA, pA' and test (pA OR pA') AND B32 with one compare and branch; stage A 36 operations per pair, 18 per batch instead of 19; hit tests at most 6 operations per stage-B entry and a 6-operation register spill per stage-C entry, both charged against the existing budgets; the set of batches entering stages B and C is unchanged). Not used: the sub-class, eight-condition rule, E1 test stage and budget premises of 60f94c5c.

Exact part: for every eight 32-bit words the two digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7 (Theorem 1), with Y4 in S8; the batches of the order S2K14 (per outer step, member, group g < 37,450 and position i < 2^14, lane l holding the trial with C2.a1 = (7g + l) 2^14 + i) cover every trial exactly once (the last group's lanes 1..6 repeat group 0 and are masked); stage A flags a lane iff its trial satisfies rule A (Lemma A3, also checked exhaustively on 2^28 cases), the pair test is taken iff some lane taking part in either batch of a pair is flagged and the hit tests send exactly the flagged batches to stage B (Lemma P), stage B iff it satisfies rule A and the beta filter (Lemma F2), and stage C computes the XOR differences of digest words 1, 3, 4 and 6 exactly (Lemmas D, D'). Every good trial (R = 0, rule A, filter) reaches stage C and is found unless a budget has halted the run.

Given H1 (ii), a budget halt (more than E - 2^14 entries) has probability below exp(-3.1 * 10^6) for stage B and exp(-1.4 * 10^5) for stage C (Theorem 2: Chernoff bound over the independent outer steps, for stage C after a union bound inside a batch; no independence inside an outer step, member, group or batch is used). Heuristic part: N = 1,057,885 * 2^80 = 2^100.01 trials.

256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with 64 registers (peak 64); seven trials per word in 36-bit lanes; stage A 18 operations for every batch (36 per pair of positions, including the pair test), stage B 66 plus at most 6 hit-test operations per entry for at most E_B = ceil(0.377 * 6001/6000 * p_B * V * 2^64 * 37,450) = 2^93.4711 batches (p_B = 0.1992731), stage C 119 plus at most 6 spill operations per entry for at most E_C = ceil(1.003 * 6001/6000 * N * 2^-11) = 2^89.0173 batches (count-down budget registers, 1 operation per entry, a halt test before each group of 2^14 batches; hit tests and stages B and C duplicated for each unrolled pair); with the block update (4 per 256 batches), group set-up, block test and end (26 per group), member step (118), X2 table (94 per word, 2^32 + 2^14 words per outer step) and outer step with its random word (274): 3.4095 operations per trial, every executed primitive including loads, stores and random words counted as 1; no sorting or lookup by value.

The time bound holds for every value of the coins. Total 2^93.045076, claimed 93.0451 (holds to 3.409537 ops/trial; budget registers in memory 2^93.0545, loop over pairs 2^93.1324; at margin 2.000, V = 1,512,538: 2^93.557577).

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word per outer step (V * 2^32 words; three 32-bit words of each are used, vc, S15 and S9; D3.d1 = X3 is fixed). Success probability 0.39 holds only under H1, the only heuristic, with parts (i) and (ii). The factor F = 132,392,960 = 2^26.9803 in H1 (i) is assumed; it is 5/7 of an exact model count of 185,350,144 (margin 1.400, disclosed), recomputed by the shipped program's --count mode, that the organizer experiments do not measure. H1 (ii) asserts, as run averages over the batches of the order S2K14 and over the trials, 0.377 times the exact model value p_B of the event that a batch enters stage B and 1.003 times the exact model rate 2^-11 of rule A with the filter; both values were set by a preregistered decision rule (two tests at 2^-64) from a uniform sample of 2^35 batches (2^37.8 trials) of this order (measured 0.376590 and 1.00006), with budgets 6001/6000 times them. With the uniform rate the same search gives about 120.2. No full collision is exhibited.

Preprocessing: a declared upper-bound charge (not a premise; H1 and the success bound do not use it) of 2^86 units (2^94.75 word operations) covers all selection of the stored constants, class, rule A, sub-class, filter, stage tests and block constants, of the order of the construction, the staged batch, the loop order S2K, the stride 2^14 and the pair test, and of the premise and budget conventions, by c66f230d, 60f94c5c, 52bb50ee, 5266c5ce, 1d5e54ce, c19feef and its predecessors and by Subflatus3, without reliance on run records (more than 2^34 times c66f230d's own estimate). Memory 2^100 bytes bounds that preprocessing by its charged work; the search itself uses under 2^42 bytes (the X2 table of an outer step under 2^41). Advice under 64 bytes.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's random words (one fresh uniform 256-bit word per outer step, supplying vc, S15 and S9; D3.d1 = X3), (i) the N = 1,057,885 * 2^80 trials of proof.md Section 4 behave, with respect to the event good (128-bit residual R = 0, rule A, and E1's c1 passes the beta filter), like independent events of probability at least F * 2^-128 each (F = 132,392,960 = 185,350,144 * 5 / 7 = 2^26.9803), to the extent that the probability that no trial is good is at most exp(-lambda) + 0.002 with lambda = N * F * 2^-128 = 0.4975807; and (ii) averaged over the V * 2^64 * 37,450 batches of the run in the order S2K14 of proof.md Section 4, the probability that a batch has a trial taking part in its decisions that satisfies rule A is at most 0.377 * p_B, and averaged over the N trials, the probability that a trial satisfies rule A and passes the beta filter is at most 1.003 * 2^-11, where p_B = 36,631,290,006,031 / 183,824,600,268,800 = 0.1992731 and 2^-11 are the exact values of these two stage events under the seven-word model M that gives the count of (i), with the distinct trials of a batch independent as in (i). The values 0.377 and 1.003 were set by the preregistered decision rule of proof.md Section 8.2 (empirical Bernstein and Lemma C' tests, each at 2^-64, on a grid of 1/1000) from a uniform sample of single batches of this order whose runs, seeds and analysis were fixed by the preregistration; no other sample or run was used to set them; the stage-B value lies below the M value because rule A clusters, and rests on that sample, not on M.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Section 4: lengths 55 and 63, the six constants of Fact P, the construction of Section 2, Y4 in the sub-class S8 of Section 3, the three words vc, S15, S9 from the outer step's own random word and D3.d1 = X3 (so X14 = 0), vd below 1,057,885, w5 and X2 over 2^32 values each, all 65,536 members; batched in the order S2K14 (per outer step, member, group g < 37,450 and position i < 2^14, lane l the trial with C2.a1 = (7g + l) 2^14 + i; the last group's lanes 1..6 masked); rule A as in Lemma A; the filter (c1 AND 00098188) = 00008000. Part (ii) concerns averages over all batches and all trials of the run, not single contexts, members, groups or batches.
heuristics.extrapolation: (i) From an exact count under the seven-word model M (proof.md Section 8.1): restricted to the six betas of T6, which the filter contains by Lemma B, the share of solutions of R = 0 with rule A among Y4 in S8 times 2^192 is 185,350,144 * 2^-128, an exact integer from 57 nonzero of 85 outcomes counted by carry automata in exact integer arithmetic without sampling (equal with and without rule A). The shipped program recomputes it: python3 experiments/s8stage.py --count (about 2 minutes). winglock's C counter, the Python port and a separately written counter agree exactly; a sampling estimator gives ratio 1.0007 +- 0.0047; every member of S8 has an exact factor of at least 184.57M; the full-class parts equal the published table of c66f230d; brute force at 8-bit words agrees. On real trials, rule-A and filter rates agree with the model at rates 2^-5 to 2^-11, the E1 part has real/model 1.0086 over 2^33.8 trials, E3 partial events of probability about 2^-38 show the counter's S8-versus-rest ratios on real trials as on model draws, and with D3.d1 = X3 the E1 events and the 2^-14 E3 event keep the rates of random D3.d1 (ratios 0.9996 to 1.0002), while the 2^-30 event on the low halves of D1 and D3 has ratio 0.82 +- 0.13 (0.87 +- 0.09 against all random-D3.d1 counts), consistent with equality (2^38 against 2^36 trials). F is exactly half of the count. (ii) Under M, h1 and c1 are independent uniform words; rule A holds for 2^27 of 2^32 words h1 and the filter for 2^26 of 2^32 words c1, so rule A with the filter has rate exactly 2^-11, and a batch of seven (last group: one) distinct independent trials has a rule-A trial with probability 1 - (31/32)^7 (1/32), giving p_B. The values of (ii) are not extrapolated from M: they are run averages estimated by uniform sampling of the run's own index space. A preregistered uniform sample of this order (proof.md Section 8.2; 34,359,738,368 i.i.d. units, 2^37.8 trials, each one batch of the run drawn uniformly: outer step with vd, w5, vc, S15, S9 uniform, D3.d1 = X3, a uniform member, group below 37,450 and position below 2^14; the sampler's batch decisions equal those of the counted program's forward computation on 27 contexts, 525,000 lanes, with verifier digests on every 50th lane) gives a stage-B share of 0.376590 +- 0.000007 of p_B (empirical Bernstein bound 0.376658 p_B at delta = 2^-64; Lemma C' exponent 1525 at the premise) and a rule-A-and-filter rate of 1.00006 +- 0.00009 of 2^-11 (empirical Bernstein 1.00096; Lemma C' exponent 72.5 at the premise); per run of 2^30 batches 0.37649 to 0.37665 p_B and 0.99927 to 1.00083 * 2^-11. The extrapolation is from this sample to the averages over all 2^100.01 trials and 2^97.6 batches of the run.
heuristics.limitations: The factor of (i) is assumed, set at 5/7 of a model count that organizer experiments do not measure (margin 1.400, disclosed). M is untested at probability 2^-100.01; real trials were compared with it for events down to about 2^-38 per trial (E1 part, E3 partial events, random D3.d1) and 2^-30 (with D3.d1 = X3) and about 2^-40 for one call in c66f230d; the full E3 event has too few hits at the sample sizes used to test. M fails inside one context for rule A (clustering); only averages are measured, and part (ii) and Theorem 2 use only such averages. The constants, class and rule A were chosen by c66f230d to maximize a count of this kind; S8 is the best under M of 8,992,320 sub-classes and supplies a factor 1.29 of the margin (the full class with rule A counts 1.555 F >= F); the filter was chosen to contain the heaviest betas; choices that are best under M may favour parameters where M overstates. 37% of the S8 count comes from one beta, 18b0e098. Trials of one outer step share its three coin words (D3.d1 = X3 in all outer steps) and trials of one context differ only in Y4; for (i) their independence is assumed. With D3.d1 = X3, X14 = 0 in every trial, so C2 runs with d = 0 and C2.d1 = ROR(a1, 16) (its outputs Y6, an E1 input, and Y14, an E3 input, still vary with X2, X6 and X10, but no longer with a coin in the d input), and X9 = S9 + X3 varies only with the coin S9; the E1 events, the 2^-14 E3 event and the 2^-30 event were measured again in this configuration (the first two equal to random D3.d1 within 0.05%, the 2^-30 event at 0.82 +- 0.13 of it, 1.4 standard errors below 1), the E1-part ratio and the per-outcome 2^-38 E3 partial events were not; H1 (i) assumes they keep their rates. Part (ii) is estimated from a uniform sample of 2^35 batches (2^37.8 trials) of this order, not from the 2^100.5 of the run, and only on the participant side with a seeded generator; the stage-B premise exceeds the observed mean by a factor 1.0011 (about 57 standard errors; 48 above the 2^-64 empirical Bernstein bound 0.376658), so it rests on the sample's size and on the correctness of the sampler (cross-checked against the counted program's forward computation of real messages on 27 contexts, 525,000 lanes, before and after freezing). One organizer run of 256 clustered seeds has a stage-B ratio with expectation about 0.377 and a large spread; one run is not evidence for or against this run average. D3.d1 = X3 changes how rule A clusters in a batch (c19feef: 0.5765 p_B against 0.6320 with random D3.d1 in the order S2K, at equal per-trial rule-A rate), and the batching changes it too (S2K 0.5765, S2K14 0.37659 for the same trials); (ii) measures it in the algorithm's configuration and order, and H1 (i) assumes it does not extend to the event good. The pair test does not change which batches enter stages B and C (Lemma P), so the premises measured for the order S2K14 apply to this algorithm unchanged. The stride 2^14 was chosen after an exploratory stride scan (disclosed with its results in proof.md Section 8.2); the premises rest only on the preregistered sample. The organizer experiments see the stage events in 17,920 clustered lanes per run. The count program runs on the participant side (about 2 minutes), not as an organizer experiment. Run selection: no organizer-run count or frequency supports F or the averages of (ii); the experiments' predictions are exact per-seed predicates; every recorded replay of the shipped program is reported (proof.md Section 6: 41 participant-run local replays with program, manifest, harness and nonces hashed before running, all exact); every run of the preregistered sample, its development runs and the stride scan are reported (proof.md Section 8.2, Run selection); no parameter, version, seed or nonce was chosen on replay or sample outcomes, and the only change after the sample is the PREMISE line set by the preregistered rule.
